content: There are various types of seizures, and some of them can be difficult to identify. If you experience any of the following signs that a seizure is occurring or might occur, stop using nafcillin and contact your healthcare provider immediately: Muscle twitching, jerking, spasms, tremors, or other uncontrolled movements. Stiffening of your arms and legs. Feelings of anxiety, nervousness, confusion, or a sense of impending doom. Dizziness or lightheadedness. Falling or losing consciousness. Nafcillin can cause kidney damage. Contact your healthcare provider immediately if you experience any of the following symptoms of kidney damage: Decreased need to urinate. Swelling in your feet, ankles, or legs. Weakness or unusual fatigue. Difficulty breathing or chest pain/pressure. Confusion. Nausea. Seizures. Nafcillin can also cause liver damage, also known as hepatotoxicity. Call your healthcare provider immediately if you experience any of the following symptoms of liver damage: Nausea or vomiting. Stomach or abdominal pain. Fever. Weakness or unusual fatigue. Itching. Loss of appetite. Light-colored stools. Dark-colored urine. Yellowing of your skin or the whites of your eyes (jaundice). Antibiotic-associated diarrhea can occur due to an overgrowth of bacteria called Clostridioides difficile (C. diff) in your gut, which can happen with many antibiotics, including nafcillin. This condition can develop even up to two months after stopping the antibiotic. Contact your healthcare provider immediately if you experience any of the following symptoms: Watery diarrhea. Persistent diarrhea that does not resolve. Blood in your stool. Severe stomach cramps. Fever that begins after starting or finishing the medication. Nafcillin can lead to blood disorders, such as agranulocytosis, neutropenia, and bone marrow depression. Stop using nafcillin and seek immediate medical attention if you experience any of the following symptoms of blood disorders: Fever. Shortness of breath. Pale or yellowish skin. Easy bruising or bleeding. Frequent infections. Unusual weakness or fatigue. Dizziness, lightheadedness, or feeling faint. Headache. Rapid or irregular heartbeat. Severe allergic reactions to nafcillin can occur. If you experience any of the following symptoms, stop using nafcillin and seek emergency medical treatment: Breathing difficulties or wheezing. Rapid heartbeat. Fever or general unwellness. Swollen lymph nodes. Swelling of the face, lips, mouth, tongue, or throat. Difficulty swallowing or a tight feeling in the throat. Itching, skin rash, or pale red bumps on the skin (hives). Nausea or vomiting. Dizziness, lightheadedness, or fainting. Stomach cramps. Joint pain. Nafcillin is typically administered by a healthcare provider in a hospital or clinic setting. If you are storing nafcillin at home, do not share it with others, even if they have the same condition, as it may harm them. Keep nafcillin out of the reach of children. Before using nafcillin, inform your healthcare provider about all your health conditions and any prescription or over-the-counter medications, vitamins, minerals, herbal products, or other supplements you are taking. This will help your provider determine if nafcillin is appropriate for you. Nafcillin may interact with other medications and supplements. Be sure to discuss the following with your healthcare provider before using nafcillin: Any allergies to penicillin, other medications, corn, or corn products. A history of asthma. Liver disease. Kidney disease. A history of antibiotic-associated diarrhea. If you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, inform your healthcare provider. It is not known how nafcillin may affect pregnancy or harm an unborn baby. Your provider will advise you on whether you should use nafcillin during pregnancy. If you are breastfeeding or planning to breastfeed, inform your healthcare provider, as nafcillin passes into breast milk. There are no known interactions between nafcillin and foods or drinks. However, it is unclear if alcohol consumption affects nafcillin. Heavy drinking can weaken your immune response and make it harder for your body to fight infections. If you accidentally use too much nafcillin, seek medical help immediately by calling 911 or contacting a Poison Control Center at 800-222-1222. Nafcillin will need to be discontinued, and a healthcare provider may treat your symptoms and provide necessary supportive care. If you miss a dose of nafcillin, use it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and only use the next dose. Do not use double or extra doses. It is important to complete your prescribed course of nafcillin, even if your symptoms improve or resolve, to reduce the risk of future infections becoming resistant to nafcillin or similar medications. The most common side effects of nafcillin include pain, swelling, and/or inflammation at the injection site, as well as rash. If these side effects bother you, inform your healthcare provider. Less common but serious side effects include severe allergic reactions, seizures, kidney damage, liver damage, blood disorders, and antibiotic-associated diarrhea. If you suspect you are experiencing any of these, contact your healthcare provider immediately.
